belief: Something is fundamentally wrong with me.
origins: Struggling with anxiety, depression, trauma, or other conditions can lead us to see ourselves as defective. Shame and comparison to “normal” people harden into a core belief that something deep inside is broken.
teaches: “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” “For He knows our frame; He is mindful that we are dust” (Psalm 103:14). “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.” Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” Struggling does not make you defective. We live in a fallen world with bodies and minds affected by it, and God’s love is not reduced by it. Help exists and healing is possible.
self_statements: Normal people do not feel this way.
Something is deeply broken in me.
I do not belong with healthy people.
errors: Believing I am either normal or defective.
Predicting that I will never be okay.
Feeling broken and concluding that I am.
questions: What does “wrong with me” actually mean?
Who taught me to see struggle as defect?
Would I call a friend with the same struggle defective?
What does God say about how I was formed?
What help have I sought or could I seek?
What strengths do I also have?
truth: I am fearfully and wonderfully made, and my struggles are not a verdict on my worth. God remembers how I am formed, loves me, and provides help. I can seek care without shame.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.
log: Each week, note one strength and one step of care.
actions: Write ten things you do well.
Talk to a doctor or counselor.
prayer: Lord, You know how I am formed. Remove my shame, give me help, and let me see myself as You do. Amen.
